yuezhuornis:study:1.title: Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans (Nature, 2026)

facts.statement: The fossil of Yuezhuornis was discovered in the summer of 2024 in the Nanyuan Formation near Yangyuan Village, Fujian Province, China.
facts.quote: The Yuezhuornis fossil material was discovered during fieldwork in the summer of 2024, in outcrops of the Nanyuan Formation near Yangyuan Village of Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China.

facts.statement: Yuezhuornis lived during the Late Jurassic (Tithonian) age.
The fossil range of Yuezhuornis spans the Late Jurassic, from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian ages.
Yuezhuornis is known from the Nanyuan Formation, dating to approximately 150 million years ago at the Kimmeridgian-Tithonian boundary.
facts.quote: Yuezhuornis is known from the Nanyuan Formation, which dates to around 150 million years ago, around the border between the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian ages of the late Jurassic period.

facts.statement: The Nanyuan Formation, where Yuezhuornis was found, represents a primarily swamp-like depositional environment.
facts.quote: The outcrops of this formation have been interpreted as representing a primarily swamp-like depositional environment.

facts.statement: The estimated body weight of the Y. yangyuanensis holotype is around 821 grams.
facts.quote: The Y. yangyuanensis holotype individual has an estimated body weight of around 821 g, derived from a calculation using the width of the femur.

facts.statement: Yuezhuornis had significantly shorter arms than its closest relatives, implying it was incapable of flight.
facts.quote: It has significantly shorter arms than its closest relatives—being proportionally more similar to many non-avialan theropods—implying it was incapable of flight.

facts.statement: The teeth in the premaxilla of Yuezhuornis are tightly packed, resembling troodontids and Anchiornis rather than Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: The teeth in the premaxilla (upper jaw bone at the front of the snout) are tightly packed, more like troodontids and Anchiornis than Archaeopteryx and other avialans, which have widely spaced teeth.

facts.statement: The furcula of Yuezhuornis has an obtuse angle, similar to Anchiornis and non-avialan paravians.
facts.quote: The furcula has an obtuse angle, as in Anchiornis and non-avialan paravians.

facts.statement: Unlike early avialans, the humerus of Yuezhuornis is shorter than the femur.
facts.quote: Also unlike early avialans, the humerus is shorter than the femur.

facts.statement: The forelimb proportions of Yuezhuornis are most similar to non-avialan paravians and flightless birds.
facts.quote: These features are most similar to non-avialan paravians (which are regarded as being incapable of flight) and flightless birds.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Yuezhuornis was secondarily flightless or if flight evolved twice within Avialae.
facts.quote: This suggests that either Yuezhuornis lost the ability for flight (thus being secondarily flightless) or that flight evolved twice within Avialae (once in Archaeopteryx and again in taxa more derived than Yuezhuornis).

facts.statement: Anatomical features support a terrestrial ecology for Yuezhuornis.
facts.quote: These features, in addition to the wide furcula, short coracoid, reduced deltopectoral crest on the humerus, and long tail, support a terrestrial ecology for Yuezhuornis.

facts.statement: Yuezhuornis is classified as an early member of Avialae.
facts.quote: Notes: An early member of Avialae.

facts.statement: Yuezhuornis is the sister taxon to Zhengheornis within the clade Zhengheornithidae.
facts.quote: Yuezhuornis was recovered as the sister taxon to the contemporary Zhengheornis, a clade Xu et al. named Zhengheornithidae.

facts.statement: Yuezhuornis diverged after Anchiornithidae and Archaeopteryx but before Baminornis within Avialae.
facts.quote: These taxa are placed within the Avialae, diverging after Anchiornithidae and Archaeopteryx, but immediately before the coeval Baminornis.
